How ADU permitting works, in plain terms

Permitting is often the least predictable part of an ADU project, because every city runs its own process. The steps below are typical, not universal.

The usual steps

  1. Site review. Confirm where the ADU can sit: setbacks, easements, utilities and lot coverage.
  2. Plan set. Floor plan, site plan, structural and energy details drawn to local code.
  3. Submission. The plan set goes to the city or county for review.
  4. Review and corrections. Reviewers often ask for changes. Fast, complete answers keep the clock moving.
  5. Permit issued. Construction can start.

HOAs and utilities

An HOA may need to approve the design separately. Utility connections can also carry their own fees and lead times. Check both early.
